newsitem.title: USA: NIMO Nine Mile Pt 2 to shut for refueling.
newsitem.headline: NIMO Nine Mile Pt 2 to shut for refueling.

text.p: The Nine Mile Point 2 nuclear plant will conclude a record run of operation Saturday when the plant is taken out of service for a scheduled refueling, Niagara Mohawk Power Corp said Thursday.
The refueling, the plant's fifth, is expected to take approximately five weeks to complete, the utility said.

Niagara Mohawk is the operator and 41 percent owner of Nine Mile Point Two, a 1,120 megawatt boiling water reactor in Scriba, N.Y. Other Nine Mile Point 2 owners include New York State Electric and Gas Corp and Long Island Lighting Co with 18 percent each.
The other owners are Rochester Gas and Electric Corp with 14 percent and Central Hudson Gas and Electric Corp with 9 percent.
The plant has been operating continuously since September 13, 1995. The refueling will end a 380 day run, the longest run since the plant began service in 1988.

During the current operating cycle, which began June 2, 1995, the plant operated 468 of 483 days and achieved a capacity factor of 96 percent. Capacity factor expresses actual output as a percent of potential maximum output of a power plant. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
